fact: NVIDIA guarantee obligations capped at $108.5 billion
why: Shown in e136 and e113's quote. Guarantees given for customers are a separate disclosure from purchase obligations and supply commitments; the rung 5 judgement does not move.

fact: NVIDIA days sales outstanding extending to 60 days
why: In e113's quote. Slower collection from customers says nothing about what NVIDIA has committed to buy from suppliers; judgement stays at rung 5.

fact: Huang: NVIDIA can supply only 70% of demand; FY2028 growth pegged about 70%
why: Same supply-capped 70% guide as e106, reworded. Supply, not demand, limits growth, so NVIDIA keeps locking in supply: supports rung 5 holding; nothing new for the judge.

fact: CFO Kress: fiscal 2028 revenue growth about 70%, a supply-constrained outlook
why: Repeat of e106 (Kress, 70%, supply-constrained). A supply-limited growth year keeps NVIDIA adding supply commitments, so rung 5 (above $200bn) is more likely to hold; nothing new.

fact: NVIDIA expects fiscal 2028 revenue growth about 70%, limited by supply constraints
why: Repeat of the guide in e106. Growth held back by supply means commitments to secure supply stay high, supporting rung 5; adds nothing the judge lacks.

fact: FY2028 growth guided about 70%; CEO says supply, not demand, holds it there
why: Judge has the same guide and that demand would allow doubling (e106). Supply as the binding limit supports commitments staying above $200bn, rung 5; nothing new.

fact: FY2028 gross margin guided 72-73% because memory prices rose more than expected
why: Verbatim in e236's quote, also e288. A margin guide is about profit; the memory-cost rise is already inside the $279bn and gives no size for year-end commitments.

fact: Huang said NVIDIA would double its chip sales next year
why: Judge has only 70% growth and a conditional 'could double'. Doubling chip sales needs far more components, so commitments more likely stay above $200bn: rung 5 firmer.

fact: NVIDIA forecasts doubling its chip volume next year
why: Judge has the 70% guide and 'could double if supply allowed', not a forecast to double volume. Twice the chips means larger supply commitments: rung 5 more likely to hold.

fact: CFO Kress: revenue up roughly 70% in fiscal 2028, limited by manufacturing capacity
why: Repeat of e106. Capacity, not demand, as the limit means NVIDIA keeps committing to supply and capacity, supporting rung 5 holding; nothing new for the judge.

fact: Nvidia expected to grow revenue at a 70% pace next year
why: Same 70% next-year growth figure the judge has in e106, here unsourced. Growth of that size keeps component purchasing and commitments high, supporting rung 5; no new information.

fact: Nvidia estimates about 70% revenue growth, labelled FY 2027 by the author
why: The author's 'FY 2027' means next year: the same 70% guide the judge has as fiscal 2028 (e106). It supports commitments staying high, rung 5; nothing new.

fact: Nvidia estimates about 70% revenue growth, labelled FY 2027 by the author
why: Syndicated copy of the same sentence; the 70% guide the judge has as fiscal 2028 (e106), period mislabelled. Supports commitments staying high, rung 5; nothing new.

fact: Management believes revenue will grow at a 70% pace next year
why: Same guide as e106; judge also knows growth could be higher if supply allowed. Supports commitments staying high, rung 5; the sandbagging remark is the author's opinion.

fact: Micron's added memory capacity will not be online until mid-2027 into 2028
why: New detail, but judge already has the CFO's supply bottleneck through fiscal 2028 and Micron's shortage; a supplier's build timing leaves rung 5 where it is.
